Contraception consultations with a pharmacist at Pacific Fair

Yes, in Queensland a trained pharmacist can prescribe the pill, the vaginal ring or the contraceptive injection for women aged 16 and over, without a GP visit. At Priceline Pharmacy Pacific Fair in Broadbeach the consultation costs $35, takes 10 to 20 minutes and happens in our private consultation room. Please call first, as trained pharmacists are usually available Monday to Friday.

Call (07) 5592 2099 Hours & directions

At a glance

What it is
A private consultation with a trained pharmacist who can prescribe the pill, vaginal ring or contraceptive injection under the Queensland pharmacy service.
Who it's for
Women aged 16 and over who want to start, restart, change or continue their contraception.
Cost
$35 consultation. Your contraception is charged separately; many types are on the PBS.
How long
10 to 20 minutes.
Booking
Please call first; trained pharmacists are usually available Monday to Friday.
How to book
Call us to book.

What can a pharmacist prescribe?

If it’s suitable for you, our trained pharmacists can prescribe:

  • the combined oral contraceptive pill
  • the progestogen-only pill (the “mini-pill”)
  • the vaginal ring
  • the contraceptive injection (ask us how the injection is given)

For longer-acting options, such as an implant or IUD, we’ll refer you to a GP. The GPs at Help Medical, an independent general practice located inside our store, offer IUD insertion.

Who can use this service?

The Queensland service is for women aged 16 and over who want to start, restart, change or continue their contraception. It became a permanent service on 1 July 2025. If the method you’re interested in isn’t the most suitable choice for you, we’ll explain why and refer you to a GP.

What happens in the consultation?

A consultation usually takes 10 to 20 minutes. Your pharmacist will:

  • go through your health and medical history, and any medicines you take;
  • check your blood pressure;
  • check your height and weight;
  • talk about your previous experience with contraception and what matters most to you;
  • explain your options, how to use your contraception correctly, and what to do if you miss a dose.

If it’s appropriate, your pharmacist can then write your prescription and dispense it for you. With your permission, we’ll send a summary to your regular GP.

How much does it cost?

The consultation costs $35. Your contraception is charged separately, and many types are listed on the PBS. There’s no Medicare rebate for pharmacist consultations.

How do I book?

Call us on (07) 5592 2099 to book. We have several trained pharmacists, usually available Monday to Friday, but consultations take a little longer and depend on a trained pharmacist being on shift, so please call first.

When would a GP be the better option?

Sometimes a GP is the better next step. For example, if something in your health history means a method may not be suitable for you, if your blood pressure reading is high, or if you’d like an implant or IUD.

Is the consultation private?

Yes. Consultations happen in a private room, and your information is handled confidentially. You’re welcome to bring a support person. For other support, see our women’s health page.

Common questions

Do I need a script from my doctor?

No. If you’re eligible, the pharmacist writes the prescription as part of the consultation and dispenses it on the spot. Call us to book.

I’m already on the pill and my script has run out. Can you help?

Yes. This service can be used to continue contraception you’re already using, if you’re eligible. Call us to book a consultation.

Is there a Medicare rebate for the consultation?

No. There’s no Medicare rebate for pharmacist consultations. The consultation costs $35, and your contraception is charged separately, with many types listed on the PBS. Ask us about the cost of your option when you book.

Can you give the contraceptive injection in store?

Our trained pharmacists can prescribe the contraceptive injection. Ask us how the injection is given when you call to book.

Can I get an implant or IUD here?

Not from the pharmacy. For longer-acting options we’ll refer you to a GP. The GPs at Help Medical, inside our store, offer IUD insertion.

Can I get emergency contraception?

Yes. The emergency contraceptive pill (the morning-after pill) is available from our pharmacists without an appointment. Ask at the counter and we’ll talk with you privately. See our emergency contraception page.
